  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Run a separate one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stimulation Paradigm as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success', which is a binary variable (0/1) based on the min=0, max=1 description, replace the ANOVA with a One-Way ANOVA equivalent such as Kruskal-Wallis test if normality fails, or proceed with ANOVA noting the distribution is discrete/binomial.",
    "Test the null hypothesis that the group means (or medians for non-parametric tests) are equal across all five stimulation paradigms for each variable.",
    "Report F-statistic (or Chi-square/Wilcoxon equivalents), degrees of freedom, and p-values for each model."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any ANOVA indicates a significant main effect (p < 0.05), perform post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's Honest Significant Difference (HSD) test.",
    "For 'Success', due to its binary nature and potential violation of ANOVA assumptions, use pairwise t-tests with correction or non-parametric equivalents if the sample sizes are balanced enough per group.",
    "Specifically compare 'Sham' against all other high-success groups ('Combined', 'Bright Visual Only', 'ICMS Only', 'Dim Visual Only') to investigate the deficit observed in the Sham group.",
    "Interpret differences in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency in the context of the success rates."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": [
    "Apply the Tukey-Kramer correction to control the family-wise error rate (FWER) across all pairwise comparisons performed within each analysis.",
    "Alternatively, use the False Discovery Rate (FDR) Benjamini-Hochberg procedure if the number of comparisons is large relative to the significance threshold and FWER control is deemed too conservative, though Tukey is standard for planned omnibus post-hocs.",
    "Set the significance level (alpha) at 0.05 for the uncorrected p-value, then apply the correction factor to the critical value or adjust the p-values."
  ],
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "A Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a Gamma distribution (and log link) is recommended for continuous, non-negative, and right-skewed variables like Time-to-Target and Average Speed, as Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression violates the normality of errors. For 'Success' (binary), a Binomial GLM (Logistic Regression) is required. Alternatively, a Multinomial Logistic Regression or a Categorical Response Model could be used if 'Stim Paradigm' were the response, but since 'Stim Paradigm' is the predictor for performance metrics, the GLM approach per variable is superior. If a joint model is desired, a Mixed-Effects Model (LMM/GLMM) with 'Mouse' as a random effect should be specified, given that 8 mice contribute repeated measures.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Assess normality of residuals for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note high skewness in Time-to-Target (sd=2.08 vs mean=2.81) and Path Efficiency (max=29.8).",
    "Check for homogeneity of variances (Levene's test) across the five stimulation paradigms; the wide range in path efficiency (0.001 to 29.8) suggests potential heteroscedasticity.",
    "Verify linearity between the continuous predictors (none, as the factor is categorical) and the responses (trivially satisfied for categorical predictors).",
    "Check for influential observations (leverage and Cook's distance), though sample sizes per group are large (e.g., n=48846 for Combined).",
    "For 'Success', verify that the proportion of successes is not too close to 0 or 1 within groups to avoid convergence issues in generalized models, although the Sham group (0.27) and others are sufficiently separated."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The ANOVA for 'Success' is expected to show a highly significant effect, with 'Sham' having a drastically lower mean (0.273) compared to all other paradigms (0.67–0.78).",
    "Time-to-Target is expected to show a significant effect, with 'Sham' having the highest mean latency (4.68s), suggesting impaired navigation efficiency.",
    "Path Efficiency and Average Speed are expected to show lower means for 'Sham' (0.31 efficiency, 10.7 speed) compared to 'Combined' and visual paradigms, indicating disrupted motor planning or speed.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) is expected to show significantly higher values for 'Sham' (0.236) compared to others, suggesting larger angular errors or less precise turning.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm is expected to yield the best trade-off metrics, followed closely by 'Bright Visual Only' and 'ICMS Only', while 'Dim Visual Only' may show slightly reduced performance compared to bright conditions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset exhibits extreme skewness in 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' (max values 201 and 29 respectively vs means ~2.8 and ~0.5), potentially violating the normality assumption of standard ANOVA.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary (0/1), making the application of standard ANOVA inappropriate without transformation or the use of generalized linear models; the provided summary uses ANOVA-style means which may be misleading for binary data.",
    "Repetitive measures from the same 8 'Mouse' IDs are not explicitly modeled in a standard one-way ANOVA, potentially inflating Type I error rates if inter-subject variance is high.",
    "The 'Sham' group (n=3505) is substantially smaller than the 'Combined' group (n=48846), which could introduce statistical power imbalances in pairwise comparisons.",
    "No information is provided regarding the distribution of 'AD' beyond mean/sd/min/max; the max of 1.0 suggests a bounded variable where ANOVA assumptions might be strained."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Perform a Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) for 'Time-to-Target' with a Gamma distribution and 'Average Speed' in both Gamma and Gaussian distributions, including 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for within-subject correlations. For 'Success', fit a Binomial GLMM. Additionally, conduct a robust non-parametric ANOVA (e.g., Brunner-Munzel test) to verify findings from the parametric tests given the heavy skewness in the data."
}
